_about: The site's changelog: one entry per day with changes, newest first. The first entry's version is the one shown in every page's footer. Version numbers: major for a redesign or rebuild, minor for days that add something new, patch for fix-only days. Each change is "new", "improved" or "fixed".

entries.title: Split rides join themselves, and a changelog

changes.text: Rides the app splits into parts, like "Bike Ride (Part 1)" and "(Part 2)" on the same day, are joined into one ride automatically, in part order.
A version number in every page's footer, linking to this changelog.

entries.title: Tidier filters, best weeks and app comparisons

changes.text: Filters are tucked behind a Filters button and start hidden; a small count shows how many are set. The Filters, Show and Columns buttons stay put when the filters open.
Each weekly goal shows your best week ever under its longest streak.
Weekly goals summary: how many weeks every goal was hit and how many goals were met this year, plus a streak badge for weeks with every goal hit.
By app / By bike chart on the Ride Log's Trends tab: distance, rides, time, average and max power and average speed, with every stat on hover.
The filter bar fits on two rows on phones when closed.

entries.title: The road book redesign: goals, routes and a world map

changes.text: A new look for every page: a light layout with a dark header showing your cumulative distance as a route profile, and a stats strip underneath.

Goals tab on both logs: weekly goals as progress rings with the last 8 weeks, streaks and longest streak, and year goals with progress bars, a pace marker, the weekly amount needed and the date each was reached.
Year goals for 2026 and 2027 with a switcher, a progress bar for the year, and a gold glint on completed goals.
Goal badges in each log's header and on the homepage cards, showing this week's and this year's goals hit.
Routes tab on the Ride Log: a world map with the countries you've ridden in, and a table by route, country or continent with flags.
Country flags next to route names; "Countries ridden in" replaces total work in the Ride Log's totals.
Trends can be grouped by week, month, 3 months, 6 months or year, with % change from the previous period and a Show menu; the Ride Log's trends add average and max power.
Columns button to hide table columns, and a Show menu for 25, 50, 100 or all rows.
The Walk Log gets the same filters, Show menu and trends as the Ride Log.
Long names scroll inside their cell so they can be read in full; every other table row is shaded.
Personal record cards get coloured stripes by type, and power records use the same purple as the table.
Walk max speeds no longer jump to impossible values from GPS glitches: max speed is now the fastest speed held for 30 seconds.
Updates show up straight away instead of browsers mixing old and new files.

entries.title: Which app each ride came from

changes.text: Each ride records the app it came from (MyWhoosh, Rouvy, Zwift, or outdoor), worked out from the device Strava reports.
Bike icons next to route names show the bike by colour and the app by a coloured ring, with a key above the table.
Filter rides by app.
A filter bar for the Ride Log: search, route, country, bike, distance, time and date range, with a count of matching rides and a Reset button.
The bike used is shown as a small coloured dot on each ride.
Renaming a bike on Strava, or changing the bike on a ride, updates it here.
Each table column can have its own width.
A ride split in two (for example when the app closed mid-ride) can be joined back into one ride, with totals added up and averages weighted by time.
The site no longer rebuilds twice after each sync.
A narrow column in the Ride Log table was cutting off values.
Changing a title, sport type or bike on Strava now updates the site; a cropped activity is downloaded again.
Syncing runs reliably every 15 minutes.
A sync that gets an empty list back from Strava can no longer wipe your saved activities.
The site becomes the Activity Log, with a homepage for picking a log and a list of recent rides and walks together.
The Ride Log moves to its own page, next to the Walk Log.
Rides and walks sync from Strava automatically every 15 minutes, with no computer needed.
A footsteps icon for browser tabs and phone home screens.
A colour theme for each page: slate for the homepage, purple for rides and green for walks.

entries.title: Strava sync and the Walk Log

changes.text: Rides now come straight from Strava instead of being typed in by hand, including power zones, heart rate and splits.
Walk Log: a page for walks and hikes with a table, graphs, records, walks vs hikes, time of day and weekly totals.
Rides can be hidden from the site, and missing details (like heart rate) filled in by hand.
Activities deleted on Strava are removed from the site.
Graphs for ride start time and running total distance.
Route names link to the ride on Strava.
The threshold zone colour is easier to tell apart from its neighbours.
Records tab: personal record cards and your time in each training zone.
Trends tab: weekly totals and a table of every route ridden.
A small zone bar on each ride in the table.
All-time bests are highlighted in the table.
Each ride shows its start time next to the date.
Removed the old script for printing rides; everything is in the web page now.
A web page listing your rides: distance, time, elevation, power, FTP, speed, heart rate, cadence, calories and effort, sortable by any column, with totals at the top.
Graphs tab with a graph for any stat over time.
